# Introduction {#introduction}

This guide provides a hands-on walkthrough for practitioners on how to use DevOps Loop for a CI-CD (Continuous Integration & Continuous Deployment) implementation.  
In this guide,  we will be using DevOps Loop for making a change in the JpetStore App \- where we try to add a new Dog category called “Bichon”.  
While doing this, we will see how CI-CD methodology can be implemented in Loop \- starting from entering a Workitem in Plan to visualising the deployment changes moving to various stages on the Measure Value stream.

# Getting started with the Loop {#getting-started-with-the-loop}

Before we deep dive into the CI-CD implementation of the JpetStore App, in this section we will review the key points involved in terms of getting started with the Loop once it is installed.  

1. ### **Installing Loop** {#installing-loop}

This document assumes that the practitioner reviewing this guide has already installed the required version of the Loop. This is the reference about the Loop installation \-\>  Installation of DevOps Loop

2. ### **Creating a new TeamSpace** {#creating-a-new-teamspace}

Once the Loop is installed, the very first step is to create a new TeamSpace.  
A teamspace in DevOps Loop is a secure, dedicated environment designed for multiple teams to work independently within a single shared DevOps Loop installation.  
When you create a teamspace in DevOps Loop, the platform automatically provisions corresponding components for all integrated applications.   
Each component is provisioned with a corresponding name that reflects the Teamspace, ensuring consistency and seamless integration across all the applications.  
Below screenshot shows the Teamspace creation in action:

![][image2]

3. ### **Creating a Loop**  {#creating-a-loop}

The loop consists of several interconnected phases that ensure continuous software development, testing, deployment, and monitoring.

Loop creation ensures seamless integration between development and operations, leading to faster and more reliable DevOps workflow. The following changes take place as a result of loop creation:

* Provisions your planning, source control, testing, deployment, and metrics tools for a ready-to-use project environment.  
* Connects all capabilities by installing and configuring essential plugins, webhooks, repositories, and integrations for real-time data sharing and visibility.  
* Provides access to a unified dashboard and links for direct access to each application.  
* Adds users in each capability and sets specific access rights across all applications.

Below screenshot shows the Loop creation in action:  
![][image3]

The initial code of the JpetStore App is deployed using the below steps: [IBM Intermediate Tutorials](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/devops-deploy/8.2.0?topic=tutorials-intermediate)

# DevOps Plan {#devops-plan}

**This guide details the IBM DevOps Plan workflow within the Loop environment, explaining how the change management process goes through its lifecycle and also tracking the source code changes associated with it.**

### **1\. Overview & Purpose :** {#1.-overview-&-purpose-:}

**DevOps Plan is a low-code/no-code sophisticated change management software designed to facilitate comprehensive change tracking and issue management. It comes with a dedicated AI assistant for enterprise-level scaling, process customization and control to accelerate project delivery and increase developer productivity.** 

**Key Objectives:**

* **Real-time collaboration: Automate workflows and use team spaces to discuss, share documents, update plans with new information, collaborate across teams, and manage stakeholders effectively.**  
* **Improved Auditability: Integrate with other products including requirements, development, build, test, deployment and portfolio management tools \- all of which help ensure a faster response to change.**  
* **Multiple workflows: Start quickly with pre-built templates for various workflows and industries, customize them to your needs, and save and share for reuse.**  
* **Task Management: Visualize tasks on an interactive board or timeline. Identify dependencies, set milestones, drag and drop tasks, and make real-time updates that trigger actions.**

### **2\. Record state transition flow** {#2.-record-state-transition-flow}

**This explains how the record is transitioned from one state to the other along with the corresponding changes:**

* **The record is created in the Submitted state.**  
* **It will need to be assigned to an owner working on that record.**  
* **Change the states of the record from source state to the destination state based on the activity being performed,**   
  * **Example: Submitted to Assigned ( when assigning this record to an owner)**  
  * **Assigned to Start (When the owner is starting to work on his code changes etc.)**

### **3\. Core Components** {#3.-core-components}

| Component | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Workflow types** | **Different workflow types are offered based on the business need.** |
| **Plan Application** | **This is an instance of a specific workflow (example: Agile / SaFe)** |
| **Backend database** | **This actually holds the data, records and its corresponding attachments.** |
| **API Server** | **This is nothing but the web server that hosts the Plan user interface.** |

### **4\. Hands-on Configuration Steps** {#4.-hands-on-configuration-steps}

After creating the Loop, the first thing is to start with the creation of a new record in Plan (or modifying an existing record) for tracking the source code changes and associating these changes with the record.  
The following steps are performed in the DevOps Plan (e.g., for Loop "**DevOp**").

1) Click on the “Plan” icon from the list of Solutions, as shown below. This will open “Plan” in a new browser tab:  
     
   ![][image6]  
 


2) You can see that a new application with the name “DevOp” is available, as highlighted. Note that the Plan application picks up the first 5 characters from the Loop name for its application name.   
   We can enter into this application by clicking on “Lets go” as shown below.   
     
   ![][image7]  
     
     
3) Now we have to create a new Workitem to capture the details of the change that is needed to be done. In our current example, we will create a workitem to add the new Dog category called “Bichon” in the JpetStore app.

   Click on the drop down menu from the right hand top corner as shown below and select the “Workitem” option:

   ![][image8]  
     
4) A new Workitem record form will open as shown below. We will fill the required fields like Title, Project, Owner, etc in the form. And finally submit the Workitem by clicking on “Save”.  
     
   ![][image9]  
     
     
5) Once the record is saved, we can see that it will have a unique ID as shown below.   
   Ex: “DevOp00000045” is created as shown below, and it will initially remain in the Submitted state.  
     
   ![][image10]  
     
     
6) We need to change the state of this record from Submitted to Backlog to start the lifecycle of continuous integration (CI). To do this, click on “Change State” drop down at the right top corner and select “Backlog” and save it:  
   ![][image11]  
     
7) Once the changes are saved, the state of the record is changed to “Backlog” as seen below:  
   ![][image12]  
     
8) Once the Workitem “DevOp00000045” is transitioned to the Backlog state, we can see the same in the Measure Value Stream. For doing this, we will select the “Measure” solution from the list as shown below.  
     
   ![][image13]  
     
9) In the Value stream, if we hover mouse over the dot, we can see the pop up showing the record ID “DevOp00000045” in the “Submitted” column.  
   ![][image14]  
     
     
10) To continue with the CI, we need to make sure the work item is assigned to an owner and the state of the record is changed from “Backlog” to “Active”. To change the state, click on “Change state” drop down again and click on “Start” as shown below:  
    ![][image15]  
      
      
    Once the record is saved, the state will be shown as “Active” on the record, as seen below:  
    ![][image16]  
    ![][image17]  
      
11) This completes the prerequisites from the Plan perspective. We will next go to the “Control” solution for making the source code changes for implementing this change.

# **DevOps Control** {#devops-control}

**This guide details the IBM DevOps Control workflow within the Loop environment, explaining how the code changes are performed in the source code and also associating these changes with the associated record in DevOps Plan.** 

### **1\. Overview & Purpose :** {#1.-overview-&-purpose-:-1}

**DevOps Control is part of DevOps Automation, a platform for software development. DevOps Control provides Git hosting, code review, and team collaboration. It is similar to GitHub, Bitbucket and GitLab. DevOps Control is based on the open-source Gitea project.** 

**Key Objectives:**

* **Code Hosting: DevOps Control supports creating and managing repositories, browsing commit history and code files, reviewing and merging code submissions, managing collaborators, handling branches, and more. It also supports many common Git features such as tags, Cherry-pick, hooks, integrated collaboration tools, and more.**  
* **Lightweight and Fast: One of DevOps Control's design goals is to be lightweight and fast in response. Unlike some large code hosting platforms, it remains lean, performing well in terms of speed, and is suitable for resource-limited server environments. Due to its lightweight design, Gitea has relatively low resource consumption and performs well in resource-constrained environments.**  
* **Security: DevOps Control places a strong emphasis on security, offering features such as user permission management, access control lists, and more to ensure the security of code and data.**  
* **Code Review: Code review supports both the Pull Request workflow and AGit workflow. Reviewers can browse code online and provide review comments or feedback. Submitters can receive review comments and respond or modify code online. Code reviews can help individuals and organizations enhance code quality.**

### **2\. Flow of the source code changes** {#2.-flow-of-the-source-code-changes}

**This explains how the source code is added / modified in the corresponding Control repository:**

* **Control repository is created by default, as a part of Loop creation.**  
* **Source code is added / modified \- Also associated with the corresponding Plan work item.**  
* **Pull requests will be created and managed.**  
* **Build will be triggered.**

| **UI frameworks** | **jQuery \- [https://jquery.com/](https://jquery.com/) Fomantic UI \- [https://fomantic-ui.com/](https://fomantic-ui.com/) Vue3 \- [https://vuejs.org/](https://vuejs.org/)**  |
| **Editors** | **CodeMirror \- [https://codemirror.net/](https://codemirror.net/) EasyMDE \- [https://github.com/Ionaru/easy-markdown-editor](https://github.com/Ionaru/easy-markdown-editor) Monaco Editor \- [https://microsoft.github.io/monaco-editor](https://microsoft.github.io/monaco-editor)**  |

# **DevOps Build**  {#devops-build}

This guide details the IBM DevOps Build process within the Loop environment, explaining how source code is transformed into deployable artifacts, how to configure the build system, and how to troubleshoot common issues.

**1\. Overview & Purpose :**  
What is Build? In the DevOps process, "Build" is the critical bridge between development and deployment. Its primary objective is to transform source code into a deployable artifact (e.g., a .war file) through automation.

As soon as new code is committed to source control, the build is automatically triggered. Each build has inputs, storage, and outputs: We can see that in the Build the Artifacts step.   
Inputs: Source code, build scripts, configuration files, and environment variables.  
Storage: CodeStation (CodeStation is an internal artifact repository).  
Output: are the generated artifacts the code is manifested into its deployable format— for example, java application as .jar, Web application as .war, Enterprise application as .ear and many more formats.zip, or Docker image.”After the build finishes, the generated artifact is automatically uploaded and becomes available for the Deploy stage.

**Key Objectives:**

* Compile & Validate: Ensure code compiles correctly.  
* Package: Create the application package (e.g., .war).  
* Store: Save the artifact immutably in CodeStation.  
* Traceability: Link the artifact version directly back to the specific Commit ID.

### **2\. The Build Flow** {#2.-the-build-flow}

The automated flow moves from the repository trigger to artifact storage:

* Repository (IBM Loop Control): A merge to the main branch triggers the process.  
* DevOps Build Server: Receives the trigger and assigns a job to an available agent.  
* DevOps Build Agent: Executes the steps defined in the Process Template (Pull source → Compile → Package).  
* CodeStation: The final artifact is published and stored here, ready for the Deployment pipeline.

### **3\. Core Components** {#3.-core-components-2}

| Component | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Repository** | **Git-based storage in IBM Loop Control. Commits here trigger the build.** |
| **Build Server** | **Orchestrates jobs, manages agents, and maintains build history/logs.** |
| **Build Agent** | **The "worker" that executes the shell scripts and compiles the code.** |
| **CodeStation** | **The built-in artifact repository that ensures versioned, immutable storage.** |

### **4\. Hands-on Configuration Steps** {#4.-hands-on-configuration-steps-2}

#### **Step vi:** Creating Job/Step Template – defines the detailed commands or scripts that run in each step of the build. {#step-vi:-creating-job/step-template-–-defines-the-detailed-commands-or-scripts-that-run-in-each-step-of-the-build.}

**Templates define the workflow.**

* Create Template: Under Templates, create a new Jobs(e.g., Job-DemoLoop\~DevOps).  
* Define Steps: Add steps to the visual workflow designer:

**Step-by-Step Breakdown**

* **1\.** **Creating Stamp:**	Create Stamp	Generates a unique build identifier (like Build\_2025\_11\_03\_01)	Used for naming versions and tracking builds  
  * **2\. Disable Control SSL:**	Shell Script	Runs a shell command to disable SSL checks or set environment flags	Useful if your build server connects to internal control with self-signed certs  
  * **3\. Cleaning Workspace:**	Clean Workspace	Deletes previous build outputs	Ensures clean environment before new build  
  * **4\. Populating Workspace:**	Populate Workspace	Pulls the latest source code from repository	Downloads repo code from GitHub/GitLab based on the trigger  
  * **5\. Get Change Logs:**	Get Source Changes	Fetches commit history since last build	Used for tracking what changed and triggering conditional builds  
  * **6\. Build the Artifacts:** we’re executing a simple shell script to compile and package our source files into a deployable artifact   
  * **7\. Upload Artifacts to CodeStation**	CodeStation \- Upload All Artifacts	Uploads the generated build output to CodeStation	Stores build outputs as versioned artifacts (immutable)  
  * **8\. Creating Component Version in Deploy for APP**	DevOps Deploy Integration	Creates a new version in UrbanCode Deploy for APP component	Makes build artifact available for deployment  
  * **9\. Creating Component Version in Deploy for WEB**	DevOps Deploy Integration	Same as above for the web tier component	Enables deployment of web service  
  * **10\. Creating Component Version in Deploy for DB**	DevOps Deploy Integration	Same for database component	Keeps all layers in sync with this build  
  * **11\. Creating Snapshot in Deploy**	DevOps Deploy Integration	Combines APP \+ WEB \+ DB component versions into one snapshot	Snapshot \= consistent set of component versions for one deployment  
  * **12\. Deploying Snapshot**	DevOps Deploy Integration	Deploys the created snapshot to the target environment	Runs the actual deployment process in UCD  
  * **13\. Waiting for Deployment**	Shell Script	Waits for deployment status (polling UCD API or logs)	Ensures job doesn’t finish before deploy completes  
  * **14\. Assigning Success**	Assign Status	Marks build as SUCCESS if all prior steps passed	Used for job reporting and triggers  
  * **15\. Assigning Failure**	Assign Status	Marks build as FAILED if any step fails	Used for error tracking and alerts

![][image45]  
 **Step vii:**Build the Artifacts: we’re executing a simple shell script to compile and package our source files into a deployable artifact — in this case, a WAR file for the JPetStore application.   
Once built, we place it inside the app/ folder so that the next step, Upload Artifacts to CodeStation, can automatically detect and upload it.   
This ensures the build artifacts are versioned and traceable within our DevOps pipeline.”  This step creates the deployable file JPetStore.war.   
The next step (Upload Artifacts to CodeStation) picks up the contents from the workspace — specifically app/JPetStore.war.   
CodeStation stores that artifact with a version number (e.g., 1.0.12). Later steps (Create Component Version In Deploy) link that version to UrbanCode Deploy components.

# DevOps Deploy {#devops-deploy}

1. ### **Overview** & **Purpose** : {#overview-&-purpose-:}

          **What is DevOps Deploy?** DevOps Deploy is an enterprise deployment solution. Use DevOps Deploy (Deploy) to standardize and simplify the process of deploying software components to each environment in your development cycle. It emphasizes collaboration between development and operations teams, aiming to accelerate software delivery and improve application quality.

2. ### **Core Functionality of Deploy** {#core-functionality-of-deploy}

* **Release Automation**: Automates the entire release process, reducing manual errors and accelerating deployments.  
* **Visibility and Traceability**: Provides comprehensive insights into application versions, environments, and configurations, ensuring compliance and auditing capabilities.  
* **Environment Modeling**: Define and manage complete application topology across multiple deployment environments.  
* **Integrations**: Offers integrations with various tools like Jenkins, Kubernetes, Microsoft, ServiceNow, and IBM WebSphere, enhancing process robustness.

### **3\. Deploy Architecture** {#3.-deploy-architecture}

* **Deploy Server**: Central hub, workflow engine, User interface, Maintain history and audit trails  
* **Agents**: Lightweight processes on target systems  
* **Repositories**: Artifacts storage  
  **Database**: Configuration and Deployment history


### **4\. Key Elements** {#4.-key-elements}

| Elements | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Applications | The overall container for your software, defining environments and processes. |
| Environments |  Logical destinations (e.g., Dev, Test, Prod) where applications are deployed, mapping to target servers. |
| Components |  Group related deployable artifacts (code, config files) and their versions.  |
| Processes | Graphical workflows (steps like install, configure, test) that automate deployment actions on components within environments. |
| Resources & Agents | Target machines (Resources) where agents are installed to execute process steps |
| Snapshots |  Collections of specific component versions known to work together, used for consistent deployments |

Additional Resources

* Elements overview: [IBM Docs \- Elements Overview](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/devops-deploy/8.2.0?topic=deploy-elements-overview)  
* Firewall and communication setup: [IBM Docs \- Firewall Configuration](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/devops-deploy/8.2.0?topic=installing-firewall-communication-configuration)

#### **5.1: Configure Deploy Service for External Communication** {#5.1:-configure-deploy-service-for-external-communication}

Overview

This guide details the steps required to configure the containerized Deploy server to accept connections from external (on-premise) agents. This involves exposing the Kubernetes service via a LoadBalancer with a static External IP and ensuring the necessary communication ports are open on the Emissary ingress.

Add External IP

1. **Determine your Kubernetes Host IP:** Use ifconfig (Linux/Mac) or ipconfig (Windows) to find the IP address of your Kubernetes host node. (Example used below: 10.190.116.49).  
2. **Identify the Kubernetes Service:** List the services to confirm the correct service name.  
*  Run \`kubectl get svc\` to list services.  
*  Identify the \`devops-loop-ibm-ucd-prod\` or ‘**devops-loop-hcl-launch-server-prod’**  service.

     Note:

  IBM Service: **devops-loop-ibm-ucd-prod**

  HCL Service: **devops-loop-hcl-launch-server-prod**


3.  Edit the Service Type:   
*      Edit the service using \`i\`.  
*      Change the service type from \`type: ClusterIP\` to \`type: LoadBalancer\`


4. Patching the Service to add External IP:  
   Run the patch command to append the externalIPs field to the service specification. Replace the IP address below with your actual Host IP.

                  $ **kubectl patch service devops-loop-ibm-ucd-prod \-p '{"spec": {"externalIPs": \["10.190.116.49"\]}}'**

   

5. Verification: Confirm that the External IP and TYPE have been successfully applied.

   $ **kubectl get svc devops-loop-ibm-ucd-prod \-o wide**

   NAME                       TYPE           CLUSTER-IP     EXTERNAL-IP     PORT(S)                         AGE   SELECTOR

   devops-loop-ibm-ucd-prod   **LoadBalancer**   10.96.96.160   **10.190.116.49**   8080:30635/TCP,7919:31531/TCP   42d   [app.kubernetes.io/component=srv,app.kubernetes.io/instance=devops-loop,app.kubernetes.io/name=ibm-ucd-prod](http://app.kubernetes.io/component=srv,app.kubernetes.io/instance=devops-loop,app.kubernetes.io/name=ibm-ucd-prod)

Expected Outpu**t:** The EXTERNAL-IP column should now display your host IP (e.g., 10.190.116.49) instead of \<none\>. You can now connect your external DB client using this IP and Port 3306\.

#### **5.2: JPetStore Application Setup** {#5.2:-jpetstore-application-setup}

# Follow IBM/HCL [IBM Intermediate Tutorials](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/devops-deploy/8.2.0?topic=tutorials-intermediate) for JPetStore, a sample app for CI/CD demos involving components, processes, resources, environments, applications, and snapshots.

# After you followed all the steps as per the document, finally you have the components are below

**DevOps-component-JPetStore-APP**  
**DevOps-component-JPetStore-DB**  
**DevOps-component-JPetStore-WEB**

![][image62]

**DevOps-component-JPetStore-APP component**

This screenshot shows the Process Design for the **`DevOps-component-JPetStore-APP`**.  
The flow follows a standard linear deployment pattern:

**Deployment Workflow Steps**

1. **Clean working directory:** Deletes existing files and directories to ensure a "fresh" environment.  
2. **Download Artifacts:** Pulls the specific version of the application code/binaries from the repository.  
3. **Unzip:** Extracts the downloaded files.  
4. **Update property file:** Modifies Java Properties files, likely injected with environment-specific variables (like DB connections).  
5. **Create .zip File:** Re-packages the updated files, potentially for archiving or final placement.  
6. **Start Tomcat:** Ensures the application server is running.  
7. **Undeploy Application:** Removes any previous version of the app currently running on the server.  
8. **Deploy Application:** Installs the new version to the server.

![][image63]

**DevOps-component-JPetStore-DB component**

This screenshot shows the Process Design for the **`DevOps-component-JPetStore-DB`**.  
This process focuses on Database Schema updates

* **Download Artifacts:** Pulls the database scripts or migration files  
* **Upgrade DB:** Executes the SQL scripts or migration commands to bring the database schema up to date with the application version.

![][image64]

**DevOps-component-JPetStore-WEB component**

This screenshot shows the Process Design for the **`DevOps-component-JPetStore-WEB`.**

* **Clean working directory:** Uses the "Delete Files and Directories" step to ensure no stale data remains.  
* **Download Artifacts:** Pulls the latest web content.  
* **Remove old content:** A secondary deletion step to target specific old directories before the new move.  
* **Deploy new content:** Uses the "Move Directory" step to place the new web assets in their final destination.

# **DevOps Test** {#devops-test}

1. ### **Overview & Purpose** {#overview-&-purpose}

![][image72]

In continuation to this demonstration, you would now focus on DevOps Test—the module that powers automation testing enabling scalable, intelligent, and collaborative quality assurance tasks.

In general, you notice that customers rely on integrating multiple tools to make a collaborative effort to perform the automation task executions. This fragmented approach does surface many challenges thereby resulting in slow innovations, creates duplication of effort, and increases delivery risk.

DevOps Test Hub helps to overcome these challenges and is built on Docker for easy deployment. You can scale your testing on cloud or on-premise systems with native Docker, Kubernetes, IBM Red Hat® OpenShift® and IBM Red Hat Enterprise Linux® support.

On the DevOps Test landing page, you need to select the respective “**TeamSpace**” which will list the projects that you have access to.  
![][image73]

The DevOps Test landing page provides a summary of the testing activities and includes multiple statistics.

![][image74]

2. ### **Recording and Execution of Tests** {#recording-and-execution-of-tests}

   

You would now see how you can execute automated tests and analyze results in real time using DevOps Test Hub capabilities. The next step in the demonstration will show this process in practice by using the recording functionality, executing the DemoTest script  and reviewing the captured results.

As part of the Loop configuration, the DevOps Test project should already be linked to the “**Control**” repository as shown below. You (Admin) may add members and assign project level permissions to the DevOps Test project.  
![][image75]

When you want to create and manage Web UI tests (Functional tests)  in DevOps Test Hub, you must first create an application within the project by navigating to “**Author** \>\> “**Test** **Editor**” and click on the “**Open** **Action Menu**” plus ( \+ ) icon 

![][image76]

Specify the application name and click the “Create” button.

![][image77]

**NOTE:**     When you want to create or modify a test resource in IBM® DevOps Test Hub (Test Hub), you must use an Edit branch. An Edit branch is a temporary branch created from the selected branch in the repository configured within the project, where you can save the created or edited resource.

You must be a Team Space Owner, Project Owner, or Member with a Tester role to create or edit a test resource. 

Now specify the application URL and description (non-mandatory field) details before clicking the “Save” icon on the right top corner.

![][image78]

Once the application is created, you can now create the test within it by clicking on the “**Create** **Test**” icon on the right top corner. Ensure that the appropriate edit branch is selected as well.

![][image79]

Upon clicking the “**Create Test**” action, you would now encounter the below window to select the appropriate application, location and  specify the test asset name. The test asset will appear in “ **.dtx.yaml**” file extension. Click “Next”.  
![][image80] 

Now the “**Select a Source**” option  provides you to either create an empty test or leverage the built-in recorder” functionality.

![][image81]

When you want to run Web UI tests authored in Test Hub on a Linux, Mac, or Windows system using an agent, you must first install and register the system as an agent by downloading and running the DevOps Test Runtime agent (**devops-test-runtime.msi** file). Select the appropriate installer packager depending on the platform where the Test hub instance is running.

![][image82]

For more information about installing the recording agent installer across various platforms, refer to the [DevOps Test Hub product documentation](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/devops-test-hub/11.0.7?topic=creation-recording-web-ui-test).

Upon selecting the browser and **UI** from the Interactions drop-down list, a new browser window is displayed and the application that you selected for recording is opened.

![][image83]

Click the UI controls and perform user actions in the application to record test steps. Ensure that you allow some delay of a few seconds between two user actions to ensure that the UI elements are recognized and registered properly.

Close the browser to stop the recording and notice that the '**The asset is now ready for your review**' message is displayed in the Create Asset dialog. Click “**Done**”

![][image84]

Your WebUI script capturing all the user actions performed on those selected UI elements is now ready to execute and generate a functional report which helps to verify that the web application performs as expected adhering to all the application changes made.

The playback execution of this test would  display a progress bar that shows the progress of the test, while the three color-coded boxes display the counts of passed steps, failed steps, and errors. You can view the step details of the first failed step or error step by clicking the respective color-coded boxes.

![][image85]

You may also navigate to the “Execute \>\> Progress” section to view the status of execution transition.  
![][image86]

### 

3. ### **Viewing Execution Results** {#viewing-execution-results}

   

Clicking on the three dots towards right side of the screen would provide you with additional options to view results in various formats

![][image87]

Clicking on the “**View** **result Overview**” would navigate you to the “**Analyze**” section providing you with the hyperlinks to open the function report or the test log details.  
![][image88]  
IBM DevOps Test Hub (Test Hub) collects the UI data during the test run and smartshots that are captured during the test run can be used to update the failed step. If an object is not identified during the test run, then the step fails. The test steps are indicated in different colors to specify the status of each test step.

The report contains a summary of the execution, the test environment, a detailed view of all tests, and the test steps that you executed.   
![][image89]  
You can see the following information in the report:

* A summary of the execution, including passed or failed status, count of passed or failed tests or test steps, and the verification points.  
* A summary of the test environment with the details of deployments, datasets, and components.  
* A detailed view of all tests that were executed in the case of an intelligent test suite, or in the case of a test with invoked tests.  
* A detailed view of all steps that were executed for each of the tests, including screenshots if any.

# **DevOps Measure** {#devops-measure}

1. ### **Overview & Purpose :** {#overview-&-purpose-:-1}

Velocity automates processes in your release lifecycle and gathers insights into your DevOps processes. It is an enterprise-scale release management service that supports both cloud-native and on-premises deployment tools. For more information about the Velocity, see [Overview of DevOps Velocity](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/SSCKX6_5.2.x/user/topics/c_overview_se.html).

2. ### **Key elements:** {#key-elements:}

| Elements | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Value Streams | A value stream represents the objects and activities that you employ to deliver customer value, from initial concept to final delivered project.The value stream provides a strategic window into your project workflow and enables you to drill-down to individual objects. The objects, such as builds, pull requests, issues, and tests, come from tools that you integrate into the value stream. Individual objects are represented graphically by small circles called dots. Dots frequently provide information from logically related tools, such as issues linked to source control commits. |
| Pipelines | Pipelines provide a streamlined method to manage the applications in your development lifecycle. With pipelines, you can auto-generate deployment plans and deploy applications versions to all environments. |
| Dots | Graphical representations of individual work items (e.g., builds, pull requests, Jira issues, or commits) that move through the value stream. |
| Integrations (Plugins) | Connections to external tools like Jenkins, Jira, GitHub, SonarQube, and ServiceNow to aggregate data into a single view. |
| Insights (Metrics) | A data-driven dashboard providing DevOps metrics (like metrics, cycle time, and lead time) to assess project efficiency and quality. |

3. ### **Hands-on Configuration Steps** {#hands-on-configuration-steps}

   Click the “Measure” icon in the Solutions list, as shown below. This will open “Measure” in a new browser tab:

![][image90]

**Measure** dashboard, shows a **Value Stream** management view. 

![][image91]

When you create a new Loop, the system provisions these distinct integration types to pull data from various stages of your delivery pipeline.

To ensure your data remains current, keep an eye on the **Status** and **Last sync** columns in your settings. Here is a quick guide on how the synchronization works:

* **Normal Operation**: All active integrations should display an **"Online"** status.  
* **Automatic Syncing**: The system is configured to perform a background sync every **5 minutes** by default.  
* **Manual Refresh**: If you need to trigger an immediate data update, you can toggle the **"Disable/Enable"** switch to force a resync.

4. ### **Breakdown of Automated Integrations** {#breakdown-of-automated-integrations}

These integrations feed the Value Stream metrics you saw earlier:

* **IBM DevOps Deploy (DeployLoops):** This connects to your deployment engine to track when code actually hits environments.  
* **DevOps Build:** Tracks CI (Continuous Integration) activity, providing data on build frequency and success rates.  
* **DevOps Control:** Likely manages the orchestration or gating data between different stages of the Loop.  
* **DevOps Plan:** Syncs with your planning tools.  
* **DevOps Test Hub:** Pulls in quality metrics and test results.

![][image92]

5. ### **Value Stream Overview** {#value-stream-overview}

When you create a new Loop, the system provisions these distinct integration types to pull data from various stages of your delivery pipeline.

The value stream visualizes the end-to-end flow of work items—such as **Tasks**, **Stories**, and **Defects**—from submission to deployment in the **DEV** environment.

**Stages of the Pipeline**

Work moves through the following stages as captured by your integrations:

* **Submitted:** New requests entering the system.  **"query": "issue.status \= \\"Submitted\\"".**  
* **Backlog :** Work prioritized and ready for development. **"query": "issue.status \= \\"Backlog\\"".**  
* **In Progress :** Active development work. **"query": "issue.status \= \\"Active\\"".**  
* **In Review:**  Under code review. **"query": "issue.status \= \\"Resolved\\" AND (pr.status \= \\"open\\" OR pr.status \= \\"review\\")"**.  
* **Completed:** Work that has finished the development/review phase.   
  **"query": "issue.status \= \\"Closed\\" AND (pr.status \= \\"merged\\" OR pr.status \= \\"closed\\") AND (deployment.env \!= \\"DEVOPS-DEV-ENV\\" AND deployment.env \!= \\"DEVOPS-QA-ENV\\" AND deployment.env \!= \\"DEVOPS-PROD-ENV\\") AND (build.status \!= \\"Failure\\" AND build.status \!= \\"success\\")"**  
* **Build Stages:**  
  * **Failed Build:** Shows Failed Build.  
     **"query": "issue.status \= \\"Closed\\" AND build.status \= \\"Failure\\" AND (deployment.env \!= \\"DEVOPS-DEV-ENV\\" AND deployment.env \!= \\"DEVOPS-QA-ENV\\" AND deployment.env \!= \\"DEVOPS-PROD-ENV\\")"**  
  * **Success Build:**   
     **"query": "issue.status \= \\"Closed\\" AND build.status \= \\"success\\" AND (deployment.env \!= \\"DEVOPS-DEV-ENV\\" AND deployment.env\!= \\"DEVOPS-QA-ENV\\" AND deployment.env\!= \\"DEVOPS-PROD-ENV\\")"**  
* **DEV :** The final stage of automation by loop, representing items deployed to the development environment.  
  **"query": "deployment.env \= \\"DEVOPS-DEV-ENV\\" AND deployment.env \!= \\"DEVOPS-QA-ENV\\" AND deployment.env \!= \\"DEVOPS-PROD-ENV\\""**  
  **QA:** Versions which are deployed on QA environment   
            **"query": "deployment.env \= \\"DEVOPS-QA-ENV\\" AND deployment.env \!= \\"DEVOPS-PROD-ENV\\""**  
* **PROD:** Versions which are deployed on PROD environment  
            **"query": "deployment.env \= \\"DEVOPS-PROD-ENV\\""**

![][image93]

You can build multiple dashboards tailored to different audiences, such as a "Quality Dashboard" for testers or an "Executive Summary" for management.
